nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the arc check of $p$ against $n$ and $E$ returns true if and only if every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ form an arc of the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ listed by $E$, that is, $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$.
nodes.title: Checking a vertex list against the arcs

nodes.summary: Given $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the arc check of a list $p$ of natural numbers returns true when every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ satisfy $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$, and false otherwise; in particular every list with fewer than two entries passes.
nodes.title: Arc check of a vertex list

nodes.summary: For every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness decoder applied to the witness encoding of $p$ (each entry $v$ written as $v$ copies of true followed by false) succeeds and returns $p$.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts the witness encoding

nodes.summary: For every list $w$ of bits and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness decoder returns $p$ on $w$ if and only if $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$, which writes each entry $v$ of $p$ as $v$ copies of true followed by false.
nodes.title: The witness codec

nodes.summary: The witness decoder succeeds on the empty list of bits and returns the empty list of vertices.
nodes.title: Decoding the empty witness

nodes.summary: If a list $w$ of bits is nonempty and reading a unary number (a run of true ended by false) from the front of $w$ fails, that is, every bit of $w$ is true, then the witness decoder fails on $w$.
nodes.title: Witness decoding fails on a cut-off first number

nodes.summary: If reading a unary number from the front of a list $w$ of bits returns $v$ with remaining bits $r$, that is, $w$ is $v$ copies of true, then false, then $r$, then the witness decoder succeeds on $w$ exactly when it succeeds on $r$, and its result on $w$ is $v$ followed by its result on $r$.
nodes.title: Decoding peels off the first number

nodes.summary: For lists $p$ and $p'$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of the concatenation of $p$ and $p'$ is the witness encoding of $p$ followed by the witness encoding of $p'$.
nodes.title: The witness encoding respects concatenation

nodes.summary: For every bit string $w$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers, if the witness decoder returns $p$ on $w$, then $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$.
nodes.title: The witness decoder succeeds only on encodings

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$, a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the HAMPATH verifier applied to the PATH encoding of $(s, t, n, es)$ and the witness encoding of $p$ returns the same boolean as the Hamiltonian path check on $n$, $es$, $s$, $t$ and $p$.
nodes.title: The verifier on an encoded instance and witness

nodes.summary: For bit strings $x$ and $w$, the HAMPATH verifier accepts $(x, w)$ if and only if there are natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$, a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers and a list $p$ of natural numbers such that $x$ is the PATH encoding of $(s, t, n, es)$, $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$, and $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ with edge list $es$.
nodes.title: What the HAMPATH verifier accepts

nodes.summary: If the PATH instance decoder fails on a bit string $x$, then for every bit string $w$ the HAMPATH verifier rejects $(x, w)$, that is, returns false.
nodes.title: Instances that do not decode are rejected

nodes.summary: If the witness decoder fails on a bit string $w$, then for every bit string $x$ the HAMPATH verifier rejects $(x, w)$, that is, returns false.
nodes.title: Witnesses that do not decode are rejected

nodes.summary: Given bit strings $x$ and $w$, the verifier decodes $x$ as a PATH instance, consisting of a start vertex $s$, a target vertex $t$, a vertex count $n$ and an edge list $E$, and decodes $w$ as a witness, a list $p$ of natural numbers each written in unary. If both decodings succeed, it accepts exactly when the Hamiltonian path check passes, that is, when $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on…
nodes.title: The HAMPATH verifier

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $s$, $t$, every edge list $E$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the Hamiltonian path check on $(n, E, s, t, p)$ returns true if and only if $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with edge list $E$.
nodes.title: The Hamiltonian path check is correct

nodes.summary: Given a natural number $n$, an edge list $E$, vertices $s$ and $t$ and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the Boolean test that $p$ has no repeated entries, has length $n$, has all entries below $n$, has first entry $s$ and last entry $t$, and that every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ satisfy $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$.
nodes.title: The Hamiltonian path check

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers all below $n$, the witness encoding of $p$ has length at most $|p| \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Witness length bound

nodes.summary: For every list $p = (v_1, \dots, v_k)$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of $p$ has length $\sum_{i=1}^{k} (v_i + 1)$.
nodes.title: Witness length

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$ and every edge list $E$, the encoding of the PATH instance $(s, t, n, E)$ has length $s + t + n + 3 + \ell$, where $\ell$ is the length of the bit encoding of the edge list $E$.
nodes.title: Length of an encoded PATH instance

nodes.summary: For every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of $p$ has length at least $|p|$.
nodes.title: A witness is at least as long as its vertex list

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
